mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the previous three months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPI increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous three months signals a tightening labor market, which leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous two months signals increased demand in the housing market, which boosts related industries and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous two months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies adjust to reduced output.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% annualized over the previous three months, the combined effect signals a tightening monetary policy with high inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy with high inflation
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over the previous two months signals increased consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the previous month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points, the combined effect signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 1% over the previous two months and GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% annualized, the combined effect signals a strong supply-side expansion, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increase > 1% and GDPC1 annualized growth > 2%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of INDPRO and GDPC1 on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
